<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD defines sources that are fetched from the project's official GitHub repository (https://github.com/nearai/ironclaw), using predictable URLs tied to a specific tag (`${_pkgname}-v${pkgver}`). The `source` array retrieves shell completion scripts via the `raw/refs/tags` path, and the binary tarballs are downloaded from the official GitHub releases page. All checksums are provided and non-SKIP, which enhances integrity, though even if they were SKIP, that would not make this stage unsafe.

The PKGBUILD does not contain any top-level command substitutions, `pkgver()` function overrides, or immediate execution of downloaded content during sourcing. The `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` command will only fetch and extract the sources, and `makepkg --printsrcinfo` only reads metadata — neither will execute the `package()` function or any build steps. There are no uses of `curl`, `wget`, `eval`, `base64`, or other dangerous constructs at global scope or in `pkgver()`. The file adheres to standard AUR packaging practices and poses no risk during the specified commands.
</details>
<evidence>

No dangerous code executes during source fetch and parse</summary>
</security_assessment>

<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD fetches prebuilt binaries and shell completion scripts from the official GitHub repository of the project (https://github.com/nearai/ironclaw), specifically from release tags. The sources are pinned to specific versions using `pkgver=1.4.0`, and checksums (`sha256sums`) are provided for all downloaded files, including architecture-specific binaries and shell scripts. There is no use of `curl`, `wget`, `eval`, `base64`, or other potentially dangerous constructs that could indicate code injection or dynamic payload retrieval.

All file installations are performed on local files extracted or copied into `$srcdir`, with proper permissions set during packaging. The binary is installed to `/usr/bin/`, and shell completions are placed in standard system directories under `/usr/share/`, which is consistent with Arch Linux packaging guidelines. No network operations, runtime modifications, or suspicious commands occur during the `package()` function.

While the sources include raw scripts fetched via `raw/refs/tags/`, these are shell completion files — not executable installers — and their integrity is protected by matching SHA-256 checksums. The use of GitHub's raw content URLs is common in AUR packages when upstream does not provide tarballs of auxiliary files. Given the presence of verified hashes and no evidence of dynamic code execution or data exfiltration, this package poses no supply-chain risk.
</details>

<details>
The provided <.SRCINFO> file is a metadata file commonly used in Arch User Repository (AUR) packages to describe the package and its sources. It declares the package base, version, architecture, license, source URLs, and checksums. All sources point to official GitHub releases or raw files from the project's own repository (https://github.com/nearai/ironclaw), which is expected and appropriate for this package.

The source files include shell scripts (bash, fish, zsh) and prebuilt binaries for x86_64 and aarch64 architectures, each with corresponding SHA-256 checksums. The checksums are provided for all sources, including architecture-specific binaries, and are not set to 'SKIP', indicating a strong level of verification. There are no signs of obfuscated URLs, suspicious network operations, or unexpected file downloads.

The package options !strip and !debug are set, which is typical for binary packages to preserve debugging information and avoid stripping symbols. This is normal for precompiled binaries and does not indicate malicious intent. Overall, the file adheres to standard AUR packaging practices and shows no evidence of supply-chain tampering or malicious content.
</details>
